subject: [PATCH v3 2/7] mm: allow shared folios to be promoted to a fast tier

2026-09-22.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from slow memory to a faster tier, but only in specific migration scenarios where the destination is top-tier (south->north). The existing restrictions for ordinary placement and non-promotion migrations remain intact. Additionally, the function name `folio_use_access_time` has been renamed to `folio_in_lowtier` to make its condition more obvious.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David noted that the patch allows promotion when there's no chance of bouncing, which aligns with the general goal of promoting if there is no east-west migration.

Reviewer David (Arm) suggested renaming the function folio_in_lowtier() to a more descriptive name, such as folio_promotable(), to make its purpose clearer and align it with the sysctl_numa_balancing_mode & NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING check.

Reviewer noted that Sashiko raised an issue with anonymous shared COW folios and expressed some agreement with their point, but did not investigate further.
sentiment_signals: reviewer did not fully understand the comment
reviewer agreed with part of it
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense. So in general we're happy to promote if there is no chance of
bouncing (as would happen with ordinary numa migration).

---

I wonder if a better name would just make the comment above (about memory
tiering) implicit and make more sense of the sysctl_numa_balancing_mode &
NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING) check.

	folio_promotable()

	folio_is_promotable()

	folio_numa_promotable()

etc.

because that seems to be what we really test with both things combined.

---

Sashiko has some comment about anonymous shared COW folios. I think it has a
point, but didn't look too closely.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that skipping the check would allow east-west migration between slow tiers, which is not intended, and described it as a 'false-positive'.
reviews.raw_body:
its tl;dr:

`skipping this check means those folios could end up freely migrating east-west
 between slow tiers`

Which cannot happen (we only migrate to top tier, numab will never
migrate *to* a slow tier).

basically false-positive

~Gregory

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges a fix is needed for the remaining issue and plans to address it in v4, but has no immediate response to David's feedback.
reviews.raw_body:
Sounds good, i'll let this rest for a bit before spinning a v4. I think
the rest is pretty solid, but there's one other sashiko thing i need to
think about whether it's real or not.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan approved the patch and gave it a 'Reviewed-by' tag.
reviews.raw_body:
folio_numab_promotable() sounds good to me.


Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from slow memory to a faster tier, as long as the migration is from south to north. This change enables promotion for low-tier folios when moving to top-tier, but maintains existing restrictions for ordinary placement and non-promotion migrations. The patch also renames the `folio_use_access_time` function to `folio_in_lowtier` to clarify its purpose.
